sections.h2: Who sends and who collects the property tax bill in Jackson County, MO?
sections.html:
Two county departments split the work. The Assessment Department values every parcel, and the Department of Collection mails the bills and takes payment. If your question is about what the house is worth on paper, call Assessment at 816-881-1330. If it is about what you owe or how to pay, call Collection at 816-881-3232.

Assessment keeps real property customer service at 1300 Washington St. in Kansas City, and individual personal property at the Historic Truman Courthouse, 112 W. Lexington in Independence. Hours at both are 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, except county holidays. Collection also works from both courthouses and answers email at Collections@jacksongov.org.

A seller in Jackson County, Missouri should pull the parcel record from the county's public property access portal before listing. It shows the assessed figures that the bill is built from.

sections.h2: What does Jackson County cover, and who lives here?
sections.html:
Jackson County sits on the Kansas border in western Missouri and has two county seats, Independence and Kansas City. It was organized on December 15, 1826, and the Missouri River forms most of its northern edge. Neighbors include Clay, Cass and Lafayette counties in Missouri and Johnson and Wyandotte counties in Kansas.

The county lists 19 communities, among them Blue Springs, Grandview, Lee's Summit, Raytown, Oak Grove, Grain Valley and Sugar Creek. Each of these sits inside the same county assessment and collection system, though a city or school district sets its own levy on the bill.

  • Land area: 604.52 square miles
  • Population estimate for July 1, 2025: 732,994
  • Housing units, same date: 344,038
  • Owner-occupied rate, 2020 to 2024: 59.1%
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $230,500

Median household income for the same five-year period is $68,577, and typical gross rent is $1,197. A homeowner with a mortgage reports median monthly owner costs of $1,639, a figure that includes the tax payment.

sections.h2: When is the Jackson County property tax bill due?
sections.html:
The bill is due on December 31. The county mails bills during November, and for 2025 the mailing was expected to finish by December 12. If nothing has arrived by about December 8, contact the Collector, since not receiving a bill does not excuse late payment.

Mailed checks need a USPS postmark of December 31 or earlier, and the county suggests mailing several days ahead because drop-box mail does not always get a same-day postmark. Checks go to the Jackson County Collector with the property account number written on them. Online payment through payments.jacksongov.org stops at 11:40 p.m. on December 31, and the two courthouse drop boxes lock at midnight that night. Cash should never go in a drop box.

Fees for paying online are a $2.00 transaction charge, plus $1.25 for an e-check or 2.75% for a debit or credit card. Paying in person or by check avoids those add-ons.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Jackson County assessment?
sections.html:
File with the Board of Equalization, an independent board of county taxpayers that now sits only at 1300 Washington in Kansas City. The 2026 application window ran until July 13, 2026, so that deadline has passed. Watch the board's page for the 2027 window.

Evidence that carries weight includes a certified appraiser's report, a sales contract with the settlement statement for a recent purchase, and written repair estimates. The board will not look at evidence shown on a phone or tablet at the hearing, and it does not make copies for you.

  • If you signed a stipulated value offered by Assessment, your board appeal is cancelled and you can no longer go to the State Tax Commission.
  • If you skip the stipulation, you keep the hearing, and a loss there can be taken to the State Tax Commission.
  • Commercial appeals to the Commission require a lawyer.
  • Withdrawing an appeal must be in writing from the homeowner and can be done any time.

sections.h2: Do I still pay the full bill while an appeal is pending in Jackson County?
sections.html:
Yes. The county tells owners to pay the bill as printed by December 31, even when a hearing is still ahead. Recalculations for 2026 appeal decisions are suspended until January 2027, and when a lower value is set, the excess is refunded automatically.

Paying under protest is optional. Missouri statute 139.031 asks for full payment before the delinquency date plus a written statement of the grounds and the value you claim. The county notes that a protest can slow a refund, since protested money is released only on a set schedule, and that protesting does not protect or harm your right to appeal. Partial payments are taken for real property, but interest, penalties and fees accrue on whatever remains unpaid after December 31, and partial payments cannot be made online.

sections.h2: Is there a cap or credit on residential assessments in Jackson County?
sections.html:
The county announced a 15% assessment cap for qualifying residential homeowners, tied to a review of the 2023 single-family assessments. Under the county's FAQ sheet dated December 8, 2025, relief arrives as a credit on the 2026, 2027 and 2028 bills, split evenly over those three years. No application is needed, no refund checks go out, and the 2025 bill still had to be paid in full.

The county says the tax money had already been distributed to schools, fire districts, libraries and cities, which is why it is a credit and not a check. The relief covers residential real estate only, and vehicles and boats are not part of it. Call Assessment if your bill looks wrong rather than assuming a credit has posted.

sections.h2: Which senior programs exist for Jackson County homeowners?
sections.html:
Two county programs apply to residential property, and an eligible owner may use both. The Senior Property Tax Credit offsets future increases. The Senior Citizen Quad Payment Program lets the owner spread the county bill over four equal installments with no interest or penalties.

  • Both require age 62 or older by December 31 of the relevant year and the home as the only primary residence.
  • The Quad program also requires prior-year taxes to be current, a home assessed solely as residential, and ownership by the person, not a trust.
  • Taxes paid from a mortgage escrow are not eligible for the Quad program.
  • The credit covers ad valorem principal only. Special assessments and CID or TDD charges are due in full.

The state Circuit Breaker credit is a separate program run by the Missouri Department of Revenue at 573-751-3505.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax bill when I sell a house in Jackson County?
sections.html:
The tax is a lien on the real estate, so it stays with the parcel and the new owner becomes liable for anything unpaid. The county explains that taxes are generally prorated between buyer and seller, with the buyer credited for the days the seller held the property that year. Normally no money goes to the Collector at the sale itself, though a closing company may pay any amount that is currently due.

Tell the Assessment office the new owner and mailing address, because a bill can otherwise go to the seller's old address. If a mortgage company pays from escrow, forward the bill to the lender. Ask the closing company which tax year it is prorating.

faqs.q: What is the last day to pay property tax in Jackson County, MO?
faqs.a: December 31. Mailed payments need a postmark on or before that date, and online payment closes at 11:40 p.m. that night. Interest, penalties and fees begin to accrue once the date passes.

faqs.q: Can I still appeal my 2026 Jackson County assessment?
faqs.a: No, the 2026 application window at the Board of Equalization ended July 13, 2026. Check the board's page next spring for the 2027 window, and pay the 2026 bill in full by December 31 in the meantime.

faqs.q: Do I need to pay under protest to get a refund after a lower value?
faqs.a: No. Refunds from a value reduction are generated automatically, and paying under protest can delay them. Protest payments must be made on time and in full with a written statement.

faqs.q: Who pays the tax when a house sells midyear?
faqs.a: The buyer owes the entire bill by December 31, and the seller's share is usually handled as a proration credit at closing. Ask the closing company how your contract splits it.

faqs.q: Where do I mail a check for Jackson County property tax?
faqs.a: Make it payable to the Jackson County Collector with the property account number on it. Protest payments go to Attention: Protest, P.O. Box 219747, Kansas City, MO 64121-9747. Call 816-881-3232 for the current regular mailing address.
